thread:
ravi: heads-up — noticed several tenants showing small persistent quota leakage in preview (~3-7 tokens/min) after we enabled the new fingerprint routing. spotted around 06:45 UTC.
jo: leakage as in unaccounted tokens or duplicate adds?
ravi: they appear as extra positive events in the tally; count never gets retracted. looks like a tiny fraction of routed requests are producing both an edge-origin fingerprint event and a canonical req-id event, and aggregator treats them as distinct.
marta: that's odd — fingerprinting was supposed to unify dedupe, not split it. any log samples?
ravi: snippet: 
```
2024-11-12T06:44:59Z INFO edge emit fingerprint tenant=T-204 fp=F:abc123 tokens=4 origin=edge-fp persisted=true
2024-11-12T06:44:59Z INFO runtime emit tenant=T-204 req=R-999 tokens=4 origin=runtime persisted=true
```
jo: fp=F:abc123 vs req=R-999 — aggregator dedupe key is (tenant, req_id) so it ignored fp events. during rollout we added fingerprint-only events for early routing telemetry but forgot to include a canonical_req_id mapping.
marta: we did that intentionally to measure early cache hits, but obviously if both are emitted we need the aggregator to treat fp events as aliases for req_id.
ravi: quick mitigation options: 1) stop persisting fingerprint-only events (edge) until aggregator supports aliasing; 2) change aggregator to dedupe on an expanded keyset (tenant + (req_id | fingerprint_aliases)). 1 is fastest.
jo: ops concern: fingerprint events are useful for routing metrics; dropping them will blind some telemetry. but leakage hurts billing. prioritize billing.
marta: agree with temporary stop. I'll prepare a small runtime flag `emit_fingerprint_metering=false` defaulting to true; flip to false in canary. also add a short-term aggregator patch that treats fp events where `fp.matches_req` if a matching req arrives within 2s mark them as duplicate rather than add.
ravi: sample aggregator pseudo diff: 
```
# on ingest event E
if E.type == 'fingerprint' and exists canonical_event within 2s with same tenant and tokens:
  mark as duplicate
else
  persist E
```
jo: be careful with race windows — 2s feels reasonable for retries/routing. add telemetry `metering.fp_aliases_deduped` to validate.
marta: will do both: flip edge flag -> canary -> if preview deltas normalize, keep off until aggregator change ships. also open PR AG-999 to add aliasing with tests.
oncall-bot: scheduled deploy: flip emit_fingerprint_metering=false -> canary 5% in 10m.
billing-bot: ALERT invoice-preview drift detected for tenants T-101,T-204,T-330 correlated with fp events.
ravi: after flip canary looked good, preview drift returns to baseline. opening follow-ups: (1) AG-999 aggregator aliasing (2) dashboard card to surface `fp_aliases_deduped` per-tenant (3) document runbook entry: "Fingerprint metering: how to handle duplicates".
jo: also add a console tooltip explaining fingerprint events vs canonical req events so CS doesn't misinterpret preview numbers.
marta: PRs: runtime #9210 (flag), aggregator #9211 (aliasing draft), docs #9212. I'll attach unit tests for race condition with 1s and 3s windows.
ravi: long-term idea: make aggregator maintain an `aliases` table mapping fp->req_id for 7 days, so fingerprint-only emissions can be reconciled back to canonical reqs post-facto during backfills. file ticket ENG-1420.
jo: +1. thanks everyone. closing when AG-999 merged. :thumbsup:
